title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Oct 9, 2026
summary: Survivors in Waso village, East Manggarai, have moved from tarpaulin tents into temporary housing built by Baznas, JPNN reported on 7 October; unit counts were not given. No new BNPB casualty or displacement release was found, so KPI totals are unchanged.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Oct 5, 2026
summary: The Ombudsman urged faster temporary housing and clean water before the November–December rains, citing 100+ people in unsuitable tents in Paralando, Manggarai. East Manggarai still had 10,140 displaced across 12 districts as of 30 September. Stage-one huntara in Manggarai stood at 109 of 385 units. KPI totals were unchanged pending a new BNPB release.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Oct 4, 2026
summary: BNPB head Suharyanto said severely-damaged-home survivors who decline temporary shelters get Rp 600,000 a month for three months while permanent housing is built. In Sikka, 1,055 household heads are covered. About 39 of 1,187 planned temporary units were complete as of 28 September. KPI totals were unchanged pending a new BNPB release.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Oct 3, 2026
summary: The Jakarta Post reported the Home Ministry will investigate deaths among quake evacuees, put at 108 in shelters against 48 direct deaths. 22,383 people remain in shelters across seven regencies. Jakarta has disbursed Rp 20 billion to each of seven local governments and Rp 40 billion to NTT province. KPI totals were not changed pending a BNPB release.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Oct 1, 2026
summary: BNPB said permanent housing for Ngada Regency victims is due by December 2026, and reiterated that temporary shelters in NTT are free of charge, with 268 units being completed in Ngada. No new official casualty totals were confirmed; reports rest on regional outlets and await BNPB confirmation.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 30, 2026
summary: BNPB's first-phase temporary-shelter build in Manggarai Regency reached 109 of 385 planned units by 29 September. West Manggarai victims were reported to be eligible for a Rp 600,000 monthly housing allowance. No new official casualty totals were published; reports rest on regional outlets awaiting BNPB confirmation.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 28, 2026
summary: Nagekeo Regency formally closed its emergency-response period on 27 September and moved into the transition phase toward recovery. About 240 evacuees remain in Riung sub-district, where bamboo-and-timber temporary shelters are being built with BNPB. No new casualty or damage totals were confirmed in this cycle; the report rests on regional outlets and awaits official confirmation.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 18, 2026
summary: BNPB began building 2,029 temporary shelters (huntara) in East Manggarai, handing over the first unit in Kampung Bugis on 17 September, and confirmed residents may self-build to spec for reimbursement. The same day, BNPB and the Ministry of Health clarified that most of the 94 deaths classified as 'indirect' involved evacuees dying of chronic-disease complications rather than earthquake trauma — the first substantive explanation of that contested classification. Manggarai Regency separately extended its own emergency status through 28 September even though the province declared recovery underway on 12 September, and NTT convened a Kupang data-consolidation forum after BNPB, BPBD NTT's Inatana app, and a third recovery-planning tally produced three diverging casualty and displacement counts for the same 15 September date.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 7, 2026
summary: BNPB chief Suharyanto briefed President Prabowo that the death toll has risen to 135, split for the first time into 48 direct and 87 indirect deaths, with 1,752 injured. Displacement plunged to 72,864 — sharply below both BNPB's own 166,829 figure and BPBD NTT's competing 96,385 count from 5 September, deepening rather than resolving the tracker's ongoing data-divergence story. Home-damage verification reached 50.39% (51,591 of 102,384 identified units), with East Manggarai recording the highest verified severe-damage count. The cumulative aftershock count hit 13,156, but weekly activity fell sharply to just 364 tremors, the clearest sign yet of the sequence tapering off. Aid distribution reached 2,142 tons via the Labuan Bajo and Maumere entry points as BNPB described health, education, economic and social activities beginning to normalize.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 6, 2026
summary: Provincial and national casualty counts diverged sharply on 5 September: BPBD NTT reported the death toll rising to 130 and displacement plunging to 96,385, while BNPB's parallel count held at 127 dead and 166,829 displaced — neither figure reconciled with the other, and the largest such gap of the response so far. Homes damaged rose to 99,568 and school damage to 2,633 per the same provincial tally. The aftershock sequence passed 12,000 events (12,438 BPBD NTT / 12,064 BNPB), including two new felt M4.6 tremors off Mbay/Nagekeo (4 Sep) and near Ruteng (5 Sep), neither causing damage. NTT Governor Emanuel Melkiades Laka Lena pledged layered oversight of incoming relief funds.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Sep 2, 2026
summary: The confirmed death toll remains unchanged at 111 since 27 August. BMKG's aftershock tally passed 10,937 events as of 1 September, with officials reaffirming a clear downward decay trend toward a forecast late-September tail-off. Recovery efforts widened beyond emergency relief: the Agriculture Ministry reported 1,321.55 tons of rice and 7,000 liters of cooking oil distributed across all seven affected regencies, Indonesia's civil aviation authority began expedited structural repairs at five quake-damaged airports (Komodo, Frans Seda, H. Hasan Aroeboesman, Soa and Frans Sales Lega), and a fuller Education Ministry breakdown found 6,927 classrooms severely damaged with 785 schools still requesting emergency classroom units.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Aug 31, 2026
summary: The confirmed death toll held at 111 for a fifth consecutive day (28-31 August, Day 17), with BNPB reporting no new fatalities. BNPB said 1,954 tons of aid — 98.39% of what it received — has now been distributed via air, sea and land routes, while the Air Force's own 729-ton, 15-day Halim Perdanakusuma relief airlift is winding down. BMKG's aftershock tally passed 10,232 events, and for the first time the agency described the decay curve as showing a clear declining pattern, though activity is still expected to continue another 3-4 weeks. Separately, the Education Ministry's assessment found 1,918 school units affected across seven regencies, with only 37 schools back to in-person classes and 295 on distance learning. Tourism recovery continued, with 7 of 18 assessed destinations and 6 of Flores' airports reopened.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Aug 28, 2026
summary: President Prabowo Subianto finally visited the earthquake zone on 26 August — eleven days after the mainshock, after two prior postponements — distributing Rp200 billion in aid across NTT province and its eight affected regencies. The confirmed death toll rose to 111 by 27 August before holding flat on Day 14 with no new fatalities reported. Displacement declined for the first time since the quake, falling from a 185,131 peak on 25 August to 176,621 on 27 August as families began returning home. BNPB's verified homes-damaged count rose to 77,912, and the agency launched an accelerated rehabilitation-reconstruction push across all seven affected regencies. Aftershocks passed 8,193.

title: Flores Earthquake Tracker Update — Aug 21, 2026
summary: BNPB and BPBD NTT raised the confirmed death toll to 83 (up from 75) as of 21 August, with displacement surging past 110,000 and homes damaged reaching 44,946. A magnitude 5.8 aftershock on 20 August triggered a fatal heart attack in Ruteng, and a previously uncounted 15 August death in Flores Timur Regency surfaced five days late, exposing a gap in the regency-level reporting system. Two cabinet ministers visited Sikka Regency on 19 August to distribute aid and condolence payments. BMKG has now recorded over 4,258 aftershocks since the mainshock.
